title: Sign-ins survive resets
summary: A reset never rolls a sign-in back to the golden's older copy. macOS keeps harness logins, browser identities and Safari's cookie store live, and quits Safari before clearing. Linux and WSL ask a running desktop Chromium to quit before clearing and keep the Claude, Codex and Cursor login files (.claude/.credentials.json, .codex/auth.json, .config/cursor/auth.json) live the same way: capture leaves them out of every golden, reset keeps them with their modes, a copy an older golden sealed is never restored, and no sign-in probe runs before clearing. A failed login is repaired by signing in again on the host. Required Linux teaching additionally keeps desktop Chromium sign-ins live outside all goldens: preserve ~/snap/chromium/common/chromium only when present, never restore its stale golden state, and quit Chromium before preservation to flush it. Reset correction 5a4b84c0d7565f38cc2308df25950fd76d4fef0e implements snap-store exclusion and conditional carry-forward and is now included in merged source 9768e3e8e225ed4120d2251eac4587ea6aa4ddd0. Earlier producer evidence was 29 targeted PASS, CI run 39040788218 PASS and QA requirement 50631 artifact 36759. Final source 6fd8127f13e7e3fa3779d9d3ca7647881dac46d7 passed full CI run 39045367272, QA requirement 50674 artifact 36808, after one authorized unchanged-index-flake rerun with original failure retained. Merged source and CI do not prove delivered or real reset/sign-in behavior; that proof remains pending. Observed status covers source observations, not live verification.
